name: swallowed-lines
description: Four non-entry lines that continue the statement above them (two now reported, two still silent), and two entries written back to back.
notes: Each of the four swallowed lines joins the statement above it, which is why the query step pins the exact joined text: reporting an error must not change how the file parses. The first two are now errors as well (an entry indented off column 0, and a space where the hyphen belongs), because 2.2.0 absorbed those in silence; spec/FORMAT.md section 9 records that change. The other two are traps v3 keeps on purpose (section 8): a heading under a statement, and an indented Status line. If a port ever reports those two, or stops parsing the swallowed lines as statement text, this case fails, which is the point. The lint step now expects one warning as well: the swallowed DEC-TRAP-002 line leaves a reference to an ID that is not an entry, so dangling_reference fires on DEC-TRAP-001.

textIncludes: DEC-TRAP-001: first rule DEC-TRAP-002: an indented ID is absorbed
DEC-TRAP-003: a space instead of a hyphen DEC-TRAP 004: is absorbed too
DEC-TRAP-005: a heading written under a statement ## Not a heading boundary
DEC-TRAP-006: an indented status line Status: Active
